properties.areaDesc: Allegheny, PA; Beaver, PA; Butler, PA; Washington, PA; Westmoreland, PA
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 11 at 9:52AM EDT until October 11 at 4:30PM EDT by NWS Pittsburgh PA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Localized flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Allegheny County in southwestern Pennsylvania...
Central Washington County in southwestern Pennsylvania...
Western Westmoreland County in southwestern Pennsylvania...
Southwestern Butler County in west central Pennsylvania...
Central Beaver County in western Pennsylvania...

* WHEN...Until 430 PM EDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall. It
will take several hours for all the water from these storms to work
through local drainage systems in urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 951 AM EDT, fire rescue personnel have reported flooding
occuring over area roadways. Between 2 and 3 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Pittsburgh, Penn Hills, Mount Lebanon, Bethel Park, Ross
Township, McCandless Township, Monroeville, Cranberry, Moon
Township, McMurray, Greensburg, McKeesport, Franklin Park,
Jeannette, Aliquippa, Canonsburg, Monaca, Vandergrift, Apollo and
Gastonville.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 11 at 9:50AM EDT until October 11 at 2:00PM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of western North Carolina, including the following
areas, Avery, Buncombe, Burke Mountains, Caldwell Mountains,
Eastern McDowell, Eastern Polk, Greater Burke, Greater Caldwell,
Greater Rutherford, Haywood, Henderson, McDowell Mountains,
Mitchell, Polk Mountains, Rutherford Mountains, Transylvania and
Yancey and Upstate South Carolina, including the following areas,
Greenville Mountains, Northern Spartanburg and Southern
Spartanburg.

* WHEN...Until 2 PM EDT this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Low-water crossings
may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rainfall tapers off behind the front, but runoff from previous
rainfall will keep high water levels in portions of the area.
Ongoing flood advisories and warnings will keep the watch in
place, even though rain has ended.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
A Flood Watch for flash flooding means there is a potential for rapid
onset flooding based on current forecasts. Flash flooding is a very
dangerous situation and may impact areas that do not typically flood.
Please monitor the latest forecasts and be prepared to take action
quickly should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

Rainfall of more than five inches in similar storms has been
associated with an increased risk of landslides, especially
fast-moving debris flows and debris slides. If you live on a
mountainside or in a cove at the base of a mountain, especially near
a stream, be ready to leave in advance of the storm and follow
evacuation orders from local officials. Consider postponing travel
along mountain roads during the heavy rainfall event.

properties.instruction:

including mudslides or flooded roads, to the National Weather Service

properties.headline: Tornado Warning issued October 11 at 9:45AM EDT until October 11 at 10:00AM EDT by NWS Raleigh NC
properties.description:
At 945 AM EDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado
was located 8 miles northeast of Wadesboro, moving northeast at 35
mph.

HAZARD...Tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed. Damage
to roofs, windows, and vehicles will occur.  Tree damage is
likely.

Locations impacted include...
Wadesboro, Lilesville, and Blewett Falls Lake.
properties.instruction:
TAKE COVER NOW! Move to a basement or an interior room on the lowest
floor of a sturdy building. Avoid windows. If you are outdoors, in a
mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter
and protect yourself from flying debris.

If a tornado or other severe weather is spotted, report it to the
National Weather Service or your local nearest law enforcement agency
who will send your report. This act may save lives of others in the
path of dangerous weather.

properties.areaDesc: Alexander, NC; Catawba, NC
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 11 at 8:42AM EDT until October 11 at 2:30PM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Alexander County in the piedmont of North Carolina...
Catawba County in the piedmont of North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 230 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to streams
and other poor-drainage areas, including farmland, parks,
greenways, boat-access areas, golf courses, underpasses, and
parking lots. Isolated, shallow flows over roadways is possible.  A
few flood-prone, low-water crossings may become impassible.  A
small culvert washout or two is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 833 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicates that an axis of torrential
rainfall is pivoting across northwestern Catawba and Alexander
counties, capable of producing accumulations of 0.75-1.5 inches
in less than 30-45 minutes.  This rainfall is occurring on top of
saturated soils due to a prolonged period of light to moderate
showers that have occurred over the county since yesterday
morning. Widespread, storm-total rainfall of the 2.5-4 inches
fell yesterday. The current torrential rainfall will cause
swollen streams to rise further, potentially exceeding their
banks and flooding adjacent low-lying areas.  Poorly-draining
areas and roadways will likely seem some flooding develop over
the next 60-90 minutes as runoff works into drainages and onto
road surfaces.

High flows will also be working down Henry Fork, Jacob Fork, and
well as the mainstem Catawba River due to upstream heavy
rainfall.  These flows may impact low-lying areas including
parks, farmland, and woodland.

- Some locations that may experience flooding include...
Hickory, Newton, Taylorsville, St. Stephens, Conover, Longview,
Bethlehem, Maiden, Hildebran and Stony Point.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become
unstable and unsafe.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...North Central San Diego County in southwestern
California...

* WHEN...Until 700 AM PDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 506 AM PDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated

area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Palomar Mountain State Park, Palomar Mountain, S7 - East Grade
Rd, Pauma Valley, Pauma Indian Reservation, Rincon Indian
Reservation and La Jolla Indian Reservation.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 11 at 5:35AM MDT until October 12 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Pocatello ID
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.
Additional amounts of 0.75 to 1.5 inches are expected with some
places pushing 2 inches.

* WHERE...Portions of central, eastern, south central, and southeast
Idaho, including the following areas, in central Idaho, Sun Valley
Region and Wood River Foothills. In eastern Idaho, Beaverhead -
Lemhi Highlands, Big Hole Mountains, Centennial Mountains - Island
Park and Teton Valley. In south central Idaho, Eastern Magic Valley
and Shoshone/Lava Beds. In southeast Idaho, Arco/Mud Lake Desert,
Bear Lake Valley, Bear River Range, Blackfoot Mountains, Caribou
Range, Franklin/Eastern Oneida Region, Lower Snake River Plain,
Marsh and Arbon Highlands, Raft River Region, Southern Hills/Albion
Mountains and Upper Snake River Plain.

* WHEN...Through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A prolonged period of rainfall is expected across eastern Idaho
throughout the weekend which could lead to some flooding across
parts of the advised area. An upper low moving into the Pacific
Northwest will combine with tropical moisture from Tropical
Cyclone Rachel to usher in a cooler, wetter weather pattern
across eastern Idaho.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Burke, NC; Caldwell, NC
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 11 at 7:28AM EDT until October 11 at 1:15PM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
FFWGSP

The National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Burke County in western North Carolina...
Caldwell County in western North Carolina...

* Until 115 PM EDT.

* At 728 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated a line of training cells
producing torrential rainfall moving across eastern Burke County
and entering central and eastern Caldwell County from the south.
This rainfall will be capable of producing 1-2 inches in less than
an hour over saturated soils. This rainfall may cause additional,
significant rises on area streams, including Zacks Fork Creek near
Lenoir; Lower Creek from Lenoir to Gamewell to Antioch Rd;
flood-prone urban areas from Cajah's Mountain to Sawmills to
Granite Falls and along US 70 from Morganton to Drexel, Valdese,
and Connelly Springs; the Yadkin River near Patterson; Kings Creek;
and Mulberry Creek near Collettsville, quickly exacerbating ongoing
Minor flooding.  Significant, Moderate flooding, potentially
impacting some structures and causing significant travel
disruptions, may develop quickly over the next 30-90 minutes.  If
you are near a creek or stream, seek higher ground now!

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life-threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams.
Expect significant flooding of adjacent low-lying areas,
including parks, trails, low-water crossings, boat-access
areas, and campgrounds.  Flooding of some crawl spaces and
basements is possible with potential flooding of
first-floors in residences and businesses near streams.
Evacuations may be needed.

* Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Hickory, Lenoir, Morganton, Longview, Sawmills, Granite Falls,
Valdese, Gamewell, Hudson and Salem.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 11 at 7:12AM EDT until October 12 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
...The Flood Advisory is extended for the following rivers in North
Carolina...

French Broad River Near at Old Fanning Bridge Rd, 3 W Fletcher
affecting Henderson and Buncombe Counties.

.Excessive runoff from a widespread 4 to 5 inch storm total rainfall
will maintain flooding along the French Broad River.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...French Broad River near at Old Fanning Bridge Rd, 3 W
Fletcher.

* WHEN...Until Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, Action Stage continues.  Glenn Bridge Park
river access is experiencing minor flooding.  Westfeldt Park is
experiencing scattered flooding.  French Broad River floodwaters
are causing isolated to widely scattered farmland flooding.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:45 AM EDT Sunday the stage was 11.2 feet and rising.
- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of around
12.0 feet just after midnight tonight.
- Action stage is 10.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 13.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
If you encounter a flooded roadway, turn around and find an
alternative route. Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

For detailed information including observed and forecast stages,
flood impacts, flood history, FEMA Flood Hazard Layers, and more,
please visit: https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/GSP

The next statement should be issued this evening before 1100 PM EDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY NOW IN EFFECT UNTIL MONDAY EVENING

properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas; San Diego County Inland Valleys; San Bernardino County Mountains; Riverside County Mountains; San Diego County Mountains; Apple and Lucerne Valleys; Coachella Valley; San Diego County Deserts; San Gorgonio Pass Near Banning
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 11 at 4:02AM PDT until October 11 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Southwest California, including the following
areas, Apple and Lucerne Valleys, Coachella Valley, Riverside
County Mountains, San Bernardino County Mountains, San Diego County
Coastal Areas, San Diego County Deserts, San Diego County
Mountains, San Diego County Valleys and San Gorgonio Pass near
Banning.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The remnants of Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel will bring periods
of moderate to heavy rain to all of San Diego County, Riverside
County mountains and deserts, and San Bernardino County mountains
and deserts through late this afternoon. Maximum hourly rainfall
rates of 0.50 to 0.60 inches per hour are possible for San Diego
Coast and Valleys. Maximum hourly rainfall rates of 0.50 to 0.70
inches per hour are possible across area deserts and 0.70 to 1
inch per hour rates are possible across area mountains. Heaviest
rainfall is most likely through early this afternoon. Rainfall
will taper off from south to north today. Lingering lighter
showers are expected to continue into Monday.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.description:

Carolina...

Henderson and Transylvania Counties.

.Excessive runoff from widespread 4 to 6 inches of storm total
rainfall will maintain flooding along the French Broad River.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...French Broad River at Grove Bridge Rd in Blantyre.

* WHEN...Until Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 16.0 feet, Minor Flood Stage. Farmland flooding
continues on both sides of the French Broad River, especially
between the river and Brevard and Pleasant Grove Roads. Floodwaters
begin to impact boat access areas at Grove Bridge Rd. and Crab
Creek Rd.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:30 AM EDT Sunday the stage was 16.0 feet and rising.
- Bankfull stage is 15.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 16.5 to
17.0 feet by this evening. It will then fall below flood stage
tomorrow.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued October 11 at 3:53AM PDT until October 11 at 3:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning through Sunday afternoon,
significant coastal flooding and beach erosion is likely. For
the Beach Hazards Statement from Sunday morning until Sunday
evening, surf of 5 to 7 feet with local sets up to 9 feet. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory from Sunday afternoon until Tuesday
afternoon, minor coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 3 PM PDT Sunday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, from Sunday morning through
Sunday evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 PM
Sunday to 2 PM PDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads and beach boardwalks may be closed
due to high water. Low-lying property including homes,
businesses, and some critical infrastructure may flood during
morning high tides. Beach erosion. Elevated surf will lead to
a high risk of rip currents and dangerous swimming conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Greatest impacts on this morning from Post-Tropical
Cyclone Rachel with a combination of increased swell, onshore
winds, and high tides locally over 7.5 feet. High tides lower
each day into the middle of the week.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Avery, NC; Burke, NC; Caldwell, NC
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 11 at 6:29AM EDT until October 11 at 1:00PM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
FFWGSP

The National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has extended
the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Avery County in western North Carolina...
Northwestern Burke County in western North Carolina...
West Central Caldwell County in western North Carolina...

* Until 100 PM EDT Sunday.

* At 629 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated a line of training cells
producing torrential rainfall entering northwestern Burke and
southeastern Avery counties.  This rainfall will be capable of
producing 1-2 inches in less than an hour over saturated soils.
This rainfall may cause additional, significant rises on area
streams, including the Linville River from Grandfather Mountain to
Linville and Pineola; Wilson Creek near Edgemont; and Warrior Fork
from Jonas Ridge to Table Rock, quickly exacerbating ongoing Minor
flooding.  Significant, Moderate flooding, potentially impacting
some structures and causing significant travel disruptions, may
develop quickly over the next 30-90 minutes.  If you are near a
creek or stream, seek higher ground now!

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life-threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams.
Expect significant flooding of adjacent low-lying areas,
including parks, trails, low-water crossings, boat-access
areas, and campgrounds.  Flooding of some crawl spaces and
basements is possible with potential flooding of
first-floors in residences and businesses near streams.
Evacuations may be needed.  An isolated landslide or two
cannot be ruled out.

* Some locations that may experience significant flash flooding
include...
Crossnore, Table Rock, Linville Falls, Lake James State Park, Jonas
Ridge and Edgemont.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

The additional heavy rain will increase the risk of landslides and
debris flows, especially in areas where landslides have occurred in
the past. Be especially alert if you live near a stream, particularly
at the base of a mountain or in a cove. Watch for signs that a
landslide may be imminent, including loose-moving soil and rocks or a
sudden increase in streamflow. Stay indoors and do NOT go outside to
investigate. Escape vertically inside your home by moving upstairs or
getting on top of counters to avoid being swept away.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 1:00 PM EDT. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 1:00 PM EDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued October 11 at 3:18AM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
HLSSGX

This product covers EXTREME SOUTHWESTERN CALIFORNIA

**THE REMNANTS OF RACHEL CONTINUE TO BRING HEAVY RAINS AND GUSTY WINDS
TO PORTIONS OF BAJA CALIFORNIA AND THE SOUTHWESTERN UNITED STATES**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- All watches and warnings have been canceled

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 90 miles east-southeast of San Mateo Point CA or about 60
miles east-northeast of Mouth of Tijuana River CA
- 32.9N 116.1W
- Storm Intensity 50 mph
- Movement North or 10 degrees at 25 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Impacts from Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel Occurred in San Diego this
morning and could continue into the early afternoon.

Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel is currently about 60 miles east
northeast of San Diego, moving north at about 25 mph. Rachel no longer
has tropical characteristics and tropical storm level impacts will
diminish in San Diego County this morning. The Tropical Storm Watch
has been cancelled for all of San Diego County. Coastal flooding,
wind, and periods of heavy rain which could lead to localized flooding
and flash flooding will continue to be a concern today. The majority
of impacts from the tropical storm have ended.

South swell from Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel will continue today. The
combination of south and northwest swells, increased onshore winds,
and high tides over 7 feet will maintain a threat of coastal flooding
and beach erosion along area beaches. Surf today is currently expected
to peak at 6 to 9 feet, decreasing to 3 to 6 feet for Monday and
Tuesday. Confidence in impactful coastal flooding is high, with
significant coastal flooding and beach erosion likely.

Widespread rain from Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel will decrease
through today. There is a gradient in rainfall amounts with the higher
amounts over San Diego County, the mountains, and parts of the low
desert. Peak rainfall rates of 0.50 to 0.80 inches were observed for
the coast and valleys, 0.50 to 0.70 inches per hour in the deserts,
and 0.70 to 1 inch per hour in the mountains. Observed rainfall totals
so far are as follows: 0.48-0.95 inches in the San Diego County
coastal areas, 0.55-2.37 for the San Diego County valleys,
0.32-2.15 for the San Diego County mountains and 0.76-1.57 for the San
Diego County deserts. Areas of flash and urban flooding occurred. The
San Diego River at Fashion Valley is currently forecast to crest at
8.1 feet (action/monitor stage) just before noon today. Those with
interests near the San Diego River should continue to monitor the
forecast.

Increased winds occurred with the onset and passage of Post-Tropical
Cyclone Rachel. Sustained winds of 59 mph were observed and stronger
wind gusts were associated with thunderstorms. The southern and
eastern parts of San Diego County saw winds of this magnitude,
although strong sustained winds and wind gusts also occurred
elsewhere. Winds were enhanced by local terrain. Winds are expected to
remain elevated in Rachel's wake with continued strong gusts on the
desert mountain slopes into the deserts through Monday morning.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Little to no additional wind impacts expected.

- Community officials are now assessing the extent of actual wind
impacts accordingly.
- Emergency response teams are attending to casualty situations
as needed.
- Emergency work crews are restoring essential community
infrastructure as necessary.
- If you have an emergency dial 9 1 1.


* SURGE:
Little to no additional surge impacts expected.

- Community officials are now assessing the extent of actual
surge impacts accordingly.
- Emergency response teams are attending to casualty situations
as needed.
- Emergency work crews are restoring essential community
infrastructure as necessary.
- If you have an emergency dial 9 1 1.


Elsewhere across EXTREME SOUTHWESTERN CALIFORNIA, little to no impact
is anticipated.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Additional impacts from flooding rain are still a concern across San
Diego County. Remain well guarded against dangerous flood waters
having further impacts of significant potential.

Additional impacts from flooding rain are still a concern across San
Diego County. Remain well guarded against locally hazardous flood
waters having further impacts of limited potential.

* TORNADOES:
Little to no impacts are anticipated at this time across EXTREME
SOUTHWESTERN CALIFORNIA.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Remain safely sheltered until conditions improve. When going outside
be sure to stay away from downed power lines, hazardous debris and
flooded areas.

If your home or shelter was damaged, be alert to the smell of gas
leaks and be cautious around electrical wiring, broken glass, jagged
metal and wood, and protruding nails and screws.

Check to see if everyone in your group is OK. Administer first aid to
those who are injured. If possible, call 9 1 1 for any serious
injuries. Remember, it may be difficult for emergency responders to
arrive quickly.

Check in with your emergency points of contact. Let them know your
location and status. Keep conversations short and to the point. Do
not tie up communications systems.

Check on your neighbors. If necessary, help them connect with their
points of contact.

Do not attempt to return to evacuated areas until local authorities
have inspected roads and bridges and have given the all clear.
Hazards like downed power lines and trees, washed out roads,
continued flooding in low lying areas and non-functioning traffic
lights make travel difficult.

Allow extra time for emergency vehicles to reach you as they navigate
road hazards.

Do not attempt to return to evacuated areas until local authorities
give the all clear. Allow time for officials to inspect bridges and
overpasses and to mark washed-out roads.

When entering areas that have been heavily damaged, bring along a
GPS-enabled device to help with street navigation. Do not drive on
roads that have been marked closed.

Do not go sightseeing within impacted communities. Sightseers
interfere with the emergency work of first responders.

When inspecting damage, use flashlights rather than candles or flamed
lanterns. Be aware of sparks that can ignite natural gas or other
leaking flammables.

Do not go up on your roof until the weather conditions are safe.
Ladders can be slippery in the rain and unexpected wind gusts can
blow you off the roof.

When clearing out fallen trees, be careful with chainsaws and axes.
Always wear protective gear and keep others at a safe distance.
Leaning trees and those which have fallen on roofs or power lines can
be especially dangerous. If you are not in good health or unsure
about what you are doing, have someone with tree cutting experience
do the job. Never cut trees without a partner.

If using a generator, avoid carbon monoxide poisoning by following
instructions provided by the manufacturer. Operate your generator in
a well-ventilated space outside of your living area and away from
open doors and windows.

Problems with sewer backups can further contaminate standing flood
waters. Keep children away from flood waters. Also, listen for boil
water alerts as tap water may have become non-potable.

Be alert for any lingering wind gusts which could take down weakened
trees and/or power lines, collapse damaged structures, or cause
flying debris.

Be alert for potential flooding from rising rivers and streams which
may have yet to crest. Remain informed of the latest river forecasts
and heed any flood watches and warnings.

Be alert for flooded roads which could be compromised or littered
with debris. Avoid travel until water levels subside and roads have
been cleared. Do not drive through places where flood waters cover
the road. Turn around, don't drown!

Have multiple ways to receive Tornado Warnings if issued. Consider
nearby shelter options as you move about. Be ready to shelter quickly.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in San Diego CA around 8 AM PDT, or sooner if conditions
warrant.

Broad River Greenway is experiencing flooding of low-elevation
trails and picnic areas along the river.  Floodwaters may be
impacting local campgrounds near the river as well.

this morning to a crest of 13.5 feet this evening. It will then
fall below flood stage late tonight.

feet on 01/25/2010.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 11 at 1:08AM PDT until October 12 at 5:00AM PDT by NWS Elko NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall and debris flows
are possible.

* WHERE...Portions of eastern, northeast, and south central Nevada,
including the following areas, in eastern Nevada, White Pine. In
northeast Nevada, the Ruby Mountains and East Humboldt Range in
Elko, South Central Elko and Southeastern Elko. In south central
Nevada, Northeastern Nye and Northwestern Nye.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams,
and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. In addition, flash
flooding is possible over recently burned areas like the former
Ward Fire, Kearny Fire, Oxley Fire, Secret Pass Fire, Starr Valley
Fire, Jones Fire, and Egberts Fire. Other burn scar locations in
the watch area could also be affected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Deep moisture from decaying Hurricane Rachel is expected to move
northward, crossing into portions of east-central and eastern
Nevada late tonight through roughly Monday. This significant
moisture will interact with upper level low pressure to bring
widespread showers with isolated thunderstorms to the watch area.
Moderate to locally heavy rain will cause excessive runoff and
may result in rock, mud, and debris flows in and near former fire
burned areas, steep terrain, and poorly drained urban areas.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.areaDesc: Coconino, AZ
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 11 at 12:58AM MST until October 11 at 8:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Moenkopi Wash in...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 800 AM MST /900 AM MDT/ Tonight.

* At 1258 AM MST /158 AM MDT/, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms
producing heavy rain over the Moenkopi Wash. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Moenkopi Wash.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Moenkopi Wash.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Tuba City and Moenkopi.

This includes the following highways...
Highway 160 between mile markers 318 and 321. U.S. Highway 89 between
mile markers 476 and 478. State Route 264 between mile markers 323
and 324.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Little Colorado River, Begashibito Wash, Hamblin Wash, Fivemile
Wash and Moenkopi Wash.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches
in the Moenkopi Wash. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated
across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. If
you encounter flood waters...climb to safety.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 8:00 AM MST. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 8:00 AM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to one half foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Kent.

* WHEN...From 7 AM this morning to 1 PM EDT this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At this level, flooding begins on the most
vulnerable roads in coastal and bayside communities, and along
inland tidal waterways. Some partial or full road closures are
possible.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 10 at 8:20PM SST by NWS Pago Pago  AS
properties.description:
ESFPPG

An active trough to the north is projected to drift southward and
move over the territory by early or midweek. This trough should
remain strong and active while over the territory, and may even
intensify with embedded low pressure centers. Widespread showers
may be heavy and persistent at times with the possibility of
thunderstorms. Widespread flash flooding may occur from this
rainfall, and landslides will be possible along steep mountainous
terrain. Impacts could begin as early as Tuesday and are expected
to persist through the weekend. While there is still uncertainty
in the exact magnitude and duration of rainfall, plan now for wet
conditions that could start as early as Tuesday and persist
through at least Sunday.

Keep up to date with the latest forecast information through our
internet page (www.weather.gov/ppg), local media, social media,
and our NOAA Radio broadcasts.

NWSheadline: Flash Flooding and landslide potential for Tuesday through Sunday

Weather Zone 009 Gogebic.

* WINDS...Southwest 5 to 15 mph with gusts up to 25 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 32 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures and
exceptionally dry fuels will create dangerous wildland fire
conditions. Campfires, outdoor grills, smoking materials,
fireworks, chain saws, and all-terrain vehicles all have the
potential to throw a spark and ignite a dangerous and destructive
fire.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 11 at 2:18AM EDT until October 11 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 8 feet in the surf zone. For the Beach Hazards Statement,
dangerous rip currents and large breaking waves expected in
the surf zone.

* WHERE...Hatteras Island beaches, and Ocracoke Island beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 8 PM EDT this
evening. For the Beach Hazards Statement, from 8 AM EDT this
morning through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water. Dangerous shore
break can throw a swimmer or surfer head first into the bottom
causing neck and back injuries.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The most likely time for strong rip
currents to occur is a couple hours either side of low tide,
which will occur around 3 PM Sunday.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Life-threatening rip currents. If caught in a rip current, remain
calm. Swim in a direction following the shoreline. If tired,
float or tread water until out of the rip current. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

Shore break occurs when waves break directly on the beach. It is
extremely important to protect your head and neck whenever you
are in breaking waves by keeping your hands in front of you at
all times.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 10 at 3:26PM PDT until October 11 at 4:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in San Diego has issued a Flood
Advisory for the following rivers in California...

San Diego River At Fashion Valley affecting San Diego County.

.Widespread moderate to locally heavy rainfall associated with
Tropical Storm Rachel over the San Diego River basin is expected
tonight into late Sunday morning. The San Diego River at Fashion
Valley is expected to peak at 8.1 ft (action/monitor stage) just
before Noon on Sunday, falling below action stage Sunday afternoon.

For the San Diego River...including Fashion Valley...elevated river
levels are forecast.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...San Diego River at Fashion Valley.

* WHEN...For Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 7.5 feet, Action stage. The first real impacts are
seen on the San Diego River at this level. Low lying roads in and
around Fashion Valley Mall begin to take on water. Avenida Del Rio
is the first road to begin flooding.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:15 PM PDT Saturday the stage was 2.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 8.1 feet
late tomorrow morning.
- Action stage is 7.5 feet.
- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

alternative route.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Sunday morning at 1000 AM PDT.

properties.areaDesc: Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 10 at 1:51PM PDT until October 13 at 2:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...DAMAGING sea-water coastal flooding is likely through
Sunday, especially near the Sunday morning high tide where
anticipated tide levels are expected to be around 8 feet. The
most likely areas for DAMAGING coastal flooding on Sunday
morning will be vulnerable southeast facing beaches, such as
Avalon and Pebbly Beach. For all other beaches and harbors,
minor to moderate coastal flooding is expected. The most
DAMAGING and WIDESPREAD coastal flooding risk along southeast
beaches will likely be with the Sunday morning high tide due to
the expected combination of very high level tide levels
approaching 8 feet (including additive effect of low barometric
pressure, high surf of 5 to 8 feet, and light to moderate
rainfall.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 3 PM PDT Sunday.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 PM Sunday to 2 PM PDT
Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Sea-water flooding of beach and harbor roads, parking
lots, and walkways is likely, especially around the time of high
tide. Isolated damage is likely across southeast facing beaches
near Sunday mornings high tide. Significant beach erosion is
expected. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides of around 8 feet are expected on
Sunday morning, returning to around 7.5 feet for Monday and
Tuesday mornings. Large secondary high tides are also expected
each evening.
properties.instruction:
Stay off of beaches and coastal walkways, roads, and structures.
Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

properties.areaDesc: Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 10 at 1:51PM PDT until October 11 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...DAMAGING sea-water coastal flooding is likely through
Sunday, especially near the Sunday morning high tide where
anticipated tide levels are expected to be around 8 feet. The
most likely areas for DAMAGING coastal flooding on Sunday
morning will be vulnerable south-facing beaches due to the
expected combination of very high level tide levels around 8
feet (including additive effect of low barometric pressure and
onshore winds gusting to 15 to 25 mph), high surf of 5 to 8
feet, and light to moderate rainfall. For all other beaches,
minor to moderate coastal flooding is expected near times of
high tide. From Sunday night through Tuesday, there will be the
continued threat of at least minor to moderate coastal flooding
and elevated surf across Los Angeles county beaches, especially
south facing shores. Dangerous rip currents are likely.

* WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 3 PM PDT Sunday.
For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM to 10 PM PDT Sunday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 PM Sunday to 2 PM PDT
Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...For vulnerable south-facing beaches (such as Alamitos
Peninsula and Naples in Long Beach as well as Malibu),
SIGNIFICANT sea- water flooding will likely DAMAGE coastal
structures and beach roadways around the time of high tide,
especially the Sunday morning high tide. In addition,
significant ponding of water on low-lying beach roadways could
make driving difficult. THERE IS GROWING CONFIDENCE THAT THE
EXPECTED COASTAL FLOODING IMPACTS ON SUNDAY MORNING FOR
VULNERABLE SOUTH FACING BEACHES OF LA COUNTY COULD BE THE MOST
SIGNIFICANT WE HAVE SEEN SO FAR THIS SEASON, INCLUDING THOSE
SEEN WITH MARIE. For all other beaches and harbors, shallow with
minor to moderate sea- water flooding will likely impact
beaches and walkways, especially with the Sunday morning high
tide which could cause local damage to most vulnerable locations
such as Venice. For all beach areas, significant erosion is
expected. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning.
Dangerous and life- threatening rip currents can pull swimmers
and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury,
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near
shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides of around 8 feet are expected on
Sunday morning (nearly 2 feet above astronomical high tide of
6.1 feet), returning to around 7.5 feet for Monday and Tuesday
mornings. The projected high tides of around 8 feet for Sunday
morning would approach or exceed recent record tide levels for
LA county. Large secondary high tides are also expected each
evening.
properties.instruction:
Follow directions of emergency officials.
Stay off of beaches and coastal walkways, roads, and structures.
Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, minor tidal overflow
flooding with elevated surf and dangerous rip currents are
expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate
coastal flooding can be expected near times of high tide,
especially with the Sunday morning high tide.

* WHERE...Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast and Santa
Barbara County Southeastern Coast.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Tuesday
afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 6 AM Sunday to
10 PM PDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Minor to moderate flooding of sea water is likely
around high tide at low-lying beach and harbor areas that is
uncommon with normal tidal ranges. Enhanced beach erosion is
possible. The risk for significant damage is very low. There is
an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats nearshore. Large
secondary high tides are also expected each evening.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides are expected to peak around 7.7
feet on Sunday morning, then 7.1 to 7.3 feet on Monday and
Tuesday mornings.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 10 at 1:51PM PDT until October 11 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT... For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate
coastal flooding can be expected near times of high tide,
especially with the Sunday morning high tide. Localized damage
is possible in most vulnerable low-lying areas. For the High
Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 8 feet with
dangerous rip currents is expected on Sunday.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 PM PDT Tuesday.
For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM to 10 PM PDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Sea-water flooding of beach and harbor roads, parking
lots, and walkways is likely, especially around the time of high
tide. Isolated damage is possible during the Sunday morning high
tide which is expected to peak around 8 feet. The most
vulnerable locations to coastal flooding will be low-lying areas
from Ventura to LA county line. Localized pockets of Highway 1
between Point Mugu and LA county line could see significant surf
spray and some sea-water on the roadway. Significant beach
erosion is expected. There is an increased risk for ocean
drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea.
Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches
and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides approaching 8 feet will be
likely on Sunday morning (nearly 2 feet above astronomical high
tide of 6.1 feet), returning to around 7.5 feet for Monday and
Tuesday mornings. Large secondary high tides are also expected
each evening.

properties.areaDesc: Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 10 at 1:51PM PDT until October 13 at 2:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...DAMAGING sea-water coastal flooding is likely through
Sunday, especially near the Sunday morning high tide where
anticipated tide levels are expected to be around 8 feet. The
most likely areas for DAMAGING coastal flooding on Sunday
morning will be vulnerable south-facing beaches due to the
expected combination of very high level tide levels around 8
feet (including additive effect of low barometric pressure and
onshore winds gusting to 15 to 25 mph), high surf of 5 to 8
feet, and light to moderate rainfall. For all other beaches,
minor to moderate coastal flooding is expected near times of
high tide. From Sunday night through Tuesday, there will be the
continued threat of at least minor to moderate coastal flooding
and elevated surf across Los Angeles county beaches, especially
south facing shores. Dangerous rip currents are likely.

* WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 3 PM PDT Sunday.
For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM to 10 PM PDT Sunday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 PM Sunday to 2 PM PDT
Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...For vulnerable south-facing beaches (such as Alamitos
Peninsula and Naples in Long Beach as well as Malibu),
SIGNIFICANT sea- water flooding will likely DAMAGE coastal
structures and beach roadways around the time of high tide,
especially the Sunday morning high tide. In addition,
significant ponding of water on low-lying beach roadways could
make driving difficult. THERE IS GROWING CONFIDENCE THAT THE
EXPECTED COASTAL FLOODING IMPACTS ON SUNDAY MORNING FOR
VULNERABLE SOUTH FACING BEACHES OF LA COUNTY COULD BE THE MOST
SIGNIFICANT WE HAVE SEEN SO FAR THIS SEASON, INCLUDING THOSE
SEEN WITH MARIE. For all other beaches and harbors, shallow with
minor to moderate sea- water flooding will likely impact
beaches and walkways, especially with the Sunday morning high
tide which could cause local damage to most vulnerable locations
such as Venice. For all beach areas, significant erosion is
expected. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning.
Dangerous and life- threatening rip currents can pull swimmers
and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury,
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near
shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides of around 8 feet are expected on
Sunday morning (nearly 2 feet above astronomical high tide of
6.1 feet), returning to around 7.5 feet for Monday and Tuesday
mornings. The projected high tides of around 8 feet for Sunday
morning would approach or exceed recent record tide levels for
LA county. Large secondary high tides are also expected each
evening.
properties.instruction:
Follow directions of emergency officials.
Stay off of beaches and coastal walkways, roads, and structures.
Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 7 AM SUNDAY TO 5 AM PDT MONDAY DUE
TO WIND AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR SHASTA METRO, N. SAC VALLEY IN
TEHAMA COUNTY, AND CENTRAL GLENN CO & INTERSTATE 5...

The National Weather Service in Sacramento CA has issued a Red Flag
Warning.

* AFFECTED AREA...Portions of the Sacramento Valley and adjacent
foothills

* TIMING...From 7 AM Sunday to 5 AM PDT Monday.

* WINDS...North to northeast winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to
30-40 mph. Strongest winds expected Sunday morning.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative Humidity between 15 to 25 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions are
either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of strong winds,
low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can contribute to
extreme fire behavior. It is important to have multiple ways to
receive information from authorities.

properties.areaDesc: Imperial County Southwest; Imperial County Southeast; Imperial County West; Imperial Valley
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued October 10 at 9:31AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...The Imperial County APCD has issued an air quality alert
due to harmful levels of particle pollution from windblown dust.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...the Imperial Valley. Levels of particle pollution can vary
by time and location depending on emissions and local weather
conditions.

* WHEN...Sunday, October 11, 2026 from 12:00 AM until 10:00 PM.

* IMPACTS... Particle pollution can get deep into the lungs and
cause serious health problems such as asthma attacks, heart and lung
disease symptoms, and increased risk of lung infections. Everyone
can be affected, but sensitive groups such as people with lung or
heart disease, older adults, people who are pregnant, children, and
those who spend a lot of time outdoors are at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, grilling, and gasoline-powered lawn and garden
equipment

To help minimize outdoor particle pollution levels:

* Carpool, telecommute, reduce trips, or take public
transportation
* Slow down if driving on dirt roads
* Stabilize loose soils
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 9 at 10:53AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
ESFGJT

A strong low pressure system off the Pacific Coast will begin to draw
in tropical moisture associated with Topical Storm Rachel this
weekend. This strong southerly fetch will draw anomalously high
moisture content across the Desert Southwest and into eastern Utah
and western Colorado. The chance for widespread precipitation
increases Saturday evening into Sunday. Total precipitation forecasts
range from 1 to 3 inches across high terrain, with highest amounts
favoring the Uintas, Tavaputs and the Southwest San Juan mountains.

Embedded thunderstorms are also possible Sunday afternoon, increasing
the threat for flash flooding across vulnerable terrain. While
confidence in location and rainfall rates remain low at this time,
the potential for rapidly rising rivers, streams, normally dry
arroyos and slot canyons are possible Sunday through Monday.

Please follow the evolving forecast, especially if your plans
including recreating or commuting across eastern Utah and western
Colorado Sunday onward. Also, keep in mind weather potential above
your location and upstream, particularly for those who reside below
sensitive terrain like recent burn scars.
